hair-oil-guide.before:
In India, oiling your hair is a weekly ritual passed down through families: warm oil massaged into the scalp, left to soak in, then washed out. It is one of the simplest ways to make dry hair feel softer and look glossier, and it is easy to start. Here is what the classic ingredients (amla, bhringraj, castor oil and more) bring to a hair oil, how to choose one, and how to oil your hair step by step.

What does a hair oil do?

A hair oil coats the hair shaft, so lengths feel softer, smoother and less frizzy, and look shinier. Used before washing, it cushions the lengths so they feel less dry after shampoo. And the scalp massage that goes with it is relaxing in itself. Think of a hair oil as a conditioning treatment for hair and scalp.

The key ingredients, explained

  • Amla (Indian gooseberry, Emblica officinalis) is the best-known ingredient in Ayurvedic hair care. In an amla hair oil, the dried fruit is steeped in a base oil such as coconut.
  • Bhringraj (Eclipta prostrata) is a herb traditionally used in Indian hair oils, often alongside amla. Bhringraj oil is usually a herbal infusion rather than a pure oil.
  • Castor oil is thick and rich. On its own it can feel heavy, so it works best mixed with lighter oils, which is how you will find it in most blends.
  • Coconut oil is the classic base for Indian hair oils, light enough for the scalp and rich enough for the lengths.
  • Hibiscus, fenugreek and curry leaf are kitchen-garden ingredients that often join amla in traditional blends.
  • Neem, tea tree and peppermint give an oil a fresh, cooling feel on the scalp.
  • Rosemary essential oil adds a herbal scent and is a popular addition to modern blends.

Our hair oils, compared

  • Deyga Hair Growth Oil (£14.99, 100ml): virgin coconut, almond, castor and sunflower oils infused with amla, bhringraj, hibiscus, fenugreek, curry leaves and other herbs, plus rosemary essential oil. A lightweight blend with an applicator tip for the scalp, and free from mineral oil and synthetic fragrance.
  • Vilvah Hair Growth Oil (£31.99, 200ml): pumpkin seed, black seed (kalonji), castor, grapeseed and almond oils with vitamin E, rosemary and peppermint. Alcohol-free and non-sticky.
  • Deyga Premature Greying Hair Oil (£18.99, 100ml): virgin coconut oil infused with amla, bhringraj, henna, bakuchi, moringa and liquorice, a classic Ayurvedic herbal blend.
  • Vilvah Anti-Dandruff Hair Oil (£19.99, 100ml): almond, neem and sesame oils with tea tree, peppermint, camphor, lemon and basil oils and amla oil, for a fresh, cooling scalp massage.
  • Deyga Neem Seed Oil (£14.99, 30ml): pure cold-pressed neem seed oil, a single ingredient. It has a strong natural smell, so most people mix a few drops into a lighter oil.

See every hair oil in one place.

A note on "hair growth" oils

Hair growth oil is one of the most searched hair care terms in the UK, and it is the name several brands give their blends (see them on our hair growth oil page). Be realistic about what any oil can do: it conditions hair and scalp, makes lengths feel softer and helps them look healthier. Hair loss has many causes, from genes to hormones, stress and diet, and no oil can change those. If you notice sudden, patchy or heavy hair loss, speak to your GP.

How to oil your hair, step by step

  1. Start with dry or slightly damp hair, before you wash it.
  2. Warm the oil. Stand the bottle in a bowl of warm water for a few minutes. Coconut-based oils turn solid in a cold bathroom; this melts them again.
  3. Part your hair into sections and apply a little oil along each parting with your fingertips or the applicator.
  4. Massage your scalp for 3 to 5 minutes with your fingertips in small circles, gently, without scratching.
  5. Smooth what is left through the lengths and ends, then comb through with a wide-tooth comb, such as a neem wood comb (£13.99).
  6. Leave it on for at least 30 minutes, or overnight with a towel over your pillow.
  7. Shampoo, and if hair still feels oily, shampoo a second time. Then condition the lengths.

Once or twice a week is plenty for most people.

Hair oil for dry hair

If your hair is dry, focus on the lengths and ends rather than the scalp, and choose a richer blend with coconut and castor oil. Between washes, smooth a single drop over the ends to tame flyaways, or use a lighter leave-in such as Vilvah Anti-Frizz Hair Serum (£28.99). More ideas: hair oil for dry hair and hair serum for frizzy hair.

Washing it out

A gentle shampoo removes oil without leaving hair squeaky and dry. Try Deyga Rice Water Shampoo (from £10.99) or Vilvah Goat Milk Shampoo (£15.99, 250ml) with goat milk, jasmine and pea protein. If your scalp tends to flake, Vilvah Herbal Shampoo for Dandruff Control (from £12.99) pairs with the Anti-Dandruff Hair Oil; see all shampoos for dandruff. If flaking or itching does not settle, ask a pharmacist.

Good to know

  • Patch test first, especially with oils that contain essential oils such as tea tree, peppermint, camphor or rosemary.
  • Keep oil away from your eyes, and do not use it on a broken, sore or irritated scalp.
  • Protect your pillow and clothes: oils can mark fabric.

how-to-use-aloe-vera-gel.before:
Aloe vera gel is one of the most searched skincare products in the UK, and it is easy to see why. One jar can work as a light moisturiser, a cooling layer after a day outdoors, a leave-in for hair and an after-shower gel for the body. Here is what to look for when you buy it, and how to use it on your face, hair and body.

What is aloe vera gel?

Aloe vera gel comes from the clear, jelly-like inside of the leaves of the aloe plant (Aloe barbadensis on an ingredient list). It is mostly water, which is why it feels so light: it sinks in quickly and does not leave a greasy film. A good gel is clear or very pale, with a soft, wobbly texture that melts when you spread it.

What to look for in a jar

  • Aloe first on the list. The first ingredient should be aloe vera juice or aloe leaf extract, not water.
  • A short ingredient list. Aloe gels need little else: a thickener to make the gel and a preservative to keep it safe once opened.
  • No added fragrance or colour if your skin is sensitive. A green tint usually means a dye has been added.

Vilvah Aloe Vera Gel (100ml, from £9.99) ticks all three. Its full ingredient list is just four items: aloe vera juice, xanthan gum, guar gum and Geogard ECT, a natural preservative. It is free from harsh alcohols, silicones and synthetic fragrance, and it is made by Vilvah, one of our official partner brands, and dispatched from the UK.

How to use aloe vera gel on your face

  • As a light moisturiser. After cleansing, smooth a pea-sized amount over damp skin. On oily or combination skin this may be all you need; on dry skin, follow with your usual cream.
  • Under your serum or cream. A thin layer first gives your routine extra slip, and serums such as Vilvah Milk Drops (from £21.99) spread easily over it.
  • As a quick mask. Apply a thicker layer for 10 minutes, then rinse or press the rest into the skin.
  • After a day outdoors. A cool layer feels comforting on skin that has had a lot of sun or wind. Keep the jar in the fridge for an extra-cool feel.

In the morning, aloe gel is not a sunscreen, so finish with SPF, such as Vilvah Skin Finish Sunscreen SPF 50 PA+++ (£17.99).

A simple routine with aloe vera gel

  1. Cleanse with a gentle face wash such as Vilvah Fragrance-Free Cream Face Wash (£9.99) or the Vilvah Honey Face Wash (£12.99).
  2. Tone with a mist of Deyga Pure Rose Water Toner (£11.99).
  3. Hydrate with aloe vera gel.
  4. Protect with sunscreen in the morning, or a richer cream at night if your skin is dry.

Prefer it ready-made? The Vilvah Sensitive Skin Kit (£29.99) pairs a steam-distilled rose toner with the aloe gel, and the Vilvah Anti-Acne Kit (£25.99) pairs the Honey Face Wash with the aloe gel for oily skin. You will find more routines on our routines page.

How to use aloe vera gel on your hair

  • As a light leave-in. Smooth a small amount through damp lengths and ends to tame flyaways and add shine without weighing hair down.
  • As a soft styling gel. Use it to smooth a ponytail or define curls, without the crunch of a styling gel.
  • With a serum. For very frizzy hair, mix a little gel with a drop of Vilvah Anti-Frizz Hair Serum (£28.99) and comb through with a wide-tooth neem wood comb (£13.99).

For more ideas, see our hair serums for frizzy hair and haircare.

How to use aloe vera gel on your body

  • After a shower, as a light, fast-drying layer on warm days.
  • After shaving or hair removal, for a cool, fresh feel on the skin.
  • Under body lotion on dry skin: let the gel sink in, then lock it in with a cream such as Vilvah Milk Body Lotion (£25.99), made with oat milk, ceramides and olive squalane.

Good to know

  • Patch test first. Apply a little to your inner arm and wait 24 hours, especially if your skin is sensitive.
  • Use clean hands or a spatula and close the jar after use, so the gel stays fresh. Check the pack for how long it lasts once opened.
  • Sunburn or a skin condition? Speak to a pharmacist or your GP. Aloe gel is a cosmetic, not a treatment.

deyga-or-vilvah.before:
If you are looking for natural skincare in the UK with roots in Indian beauty traditions, two names come up again and again: Deyga and Vilvah. Both are Indian brands, both work with plant-based and kitchen-cupboard ingredients, and Swansura is an official UK partner of both, so every product is genuine and ships from the UK. They are not the same, though. Here is how to tell which one suits your skin, and where to start.

The short answer

Choose Vilvah if you like creamy, comforting textures built around goat milk, oat milk and gentle botanicals. Choose Deyga if you prefer farm-grown herbs, clays, charcoal and fruit actives with a fresher feel. Many people end up using both: a Vilvah cleanser or serum in the morning and a Deyga treat, such as a lip balm or face pack, alongside it.

Vilvah: goat milk and botanical care

Vilvah is known for milk-based formulas for face, hair and body. The best place to start is Vilvah Milk Drops Hydrating Serum, a lightweight milk serum with natural milk proteins that sinks in quickly and leaves skin feeling soft rather than greasy. It is the product people search for most: "Vilvah Milk Drops" is one of the brand's top searches in the UK.

For hair, the Vilvah Goat Milk Shampoo pairs goat milk with pea protein and jasmine. It is pH-balanced and free from artificial colours and fragrances, so it suits frequent washing, and it is a good fit for dry or frizzy hair. If you want the full ritual, the Goat Milk Hair Kit puts the shampoo with its partners in one box.

For the body, Vilvah Milk Body Lotion uses oat milk, ceramides and olive squalane in a quick-absorbing, vegan formula that is gentle enough for the whole family. Prefer a no-scent wash? The Fragrance-Free Cream Face Wash is the calmest place to begin. See the whole range on our goat milk edit.

Deyga: farm-grown botanicals

Deyga makes natural skin, hair and body care with plant-based ingredients, many grown on its own farm in India. Its cult favourite is the Deyga Beetroot Lip Balm: beetroot extract and natural butters give a soft, sheer tint, and the 10 g tin fits any pocket. "Deyga lip balm" is one of the brand's most searched products, and it makes an easy first try at under £11.

For oilier or combination skin, the Deyga Charcoal Face Wash uses activated charcoal for a deep, refreshing cleanse without a tight finish. For glow, the Deyga Rose Glow Serum is a light rose and saffron oil serum that leaves skin looking radiant. On wash day, Deyga Rice Water Shampoo is a gentle, sulfate-free everyday cleanser.

Which is better for your skin type?

Dry or sensitive skin

Lean towards Vilvah. Milk textures, fragrance-free options and the oat milk body lotion are made for comfort. Add a Deyga body butter for dry skin, such as the Chocolate Body Butter, for extra richness on elbows and legs.

Oily or combination skin

Start with Deyga's charcoal face wash and a lightweight serum, then use a Vilvah milk product only where skin feels dry. Our face wash for oily skin page compares the options side by side.

Dull-looking skin

Try one serum from each brand on alternate days: Vilvah Milk Drops for hydration and Deyga Rose Glow for radiance. Keep everything else simple.

A simple routine using both brands

  1. Cleanse: Deyga Charcoal Face Wash (oilier skin) or Vilvah Fragrance-Free Cream Face Wash (drier skin).
  2. Treat: Vilvah Milk Drops in the morning, Deyga Rose Glow in the evening.
  3. Lips and body: Deyga Beetroot Lip Balm through the day and Vilvah Milk Body Lotion after showering.

Patch test anything new and introduce one product at a time. Ready-made pairings with 5% off are on our routines page.

Why buy Deyga and Vilvah from Swansura?

We are an official UK partner of both brands, so there are no grey imports and no long waits from abroad: orders are dispatched from the UK, usually within 1–2 working days, with free UK delivery over £40. Explore the full natural skincare edit, or go straight to all Deyga and all Vilvah products.
